name: STE-NOTES-1-sentence-26
note: A sentence of 26 words would pass - STE allows 25.

name: STE-NOTES-2-instruction-21
note: An instruction of 21 words would pass - STE allows 20.

name: STE-NOTES-3-paragraph-7
note: A paragraph of seven sentences would pass - STE allows six.

name: STE-NOTES-4-condition-not-first
note: An instruction with its condition put first, as STE writes it, would be read as a sentence of 25.

name: STE-NOTES-5-unit-a-word
note: A number and its unit would count as two words.

name: STE-NOTES-6-bold-read
note: A control marked bold would count word by word, and be read for -ing forms.

name: STE-NOTES-7-quotes-read
note: A quoted label would count word by word.

name: STE-NOTES-8-code-read
note: A semicolon inside `code` would be the writer's.

name: STE-NOTES-9-eg-ends
note: "e.g." would end a sentence.

name: STE-NOTES-10-semicolon-blind
note: A semicolon would pass.

name: STE-NOTES-11-head-capital-a-name
note: "Picking" at the head of a sentence would be taken for a name.

name: STE-NOTES-12-heading-capitals-read
note: A sub-heading that is a name ("### Gathering") would be read as a verb.

name: STE-NOTES-13-hyphen-whole
note: "hard-hitting" would pass.

name: STE-NOTES-14-nouns-read
note: "Nothing", "setting" and "during" would be read as verbs.

name: STE-NOTES-15-curly-apostrophe
note: "can’t" with a curly apostrophe would pass.

name: STE-NOTES-16-possessive-a-contraction
note: A possessive ("the player's gear") would be a contraction.

name: STE-NOTES-17-regular-unread
note: "We have fixed a bug" would pass.

name: STE-NOTES-18-adjective-a-verb
note: "Some chests have enchanted items" would be a complex verb.

name: STE-NOTES-19-hit-points
note: "Ships have hit points" would be a complex verb.

name: STE-NOTES-20-built-in
note: "Swords have built-in sigils" would be a complex verb.

name: STE-NOTES-21-whole-description
note: The reviewers' sections would be read as notes.

name: STE-NOTES-22-items-run-on
note: A new list item would run on in the item before it.

name: STE-NOTES-23-blank-joins
note: A blank line would not end a paragraph.

name: STE-NOTES-24-continuation-new
old:
if (open) open.text += ` ${body.trim()}`;
    else open = { heading: false, text: body.trim() };
new:
close();
    open = { heading: false, text: body.trim() };
note: An item's indented line would be a paragraph of its own.

name: STE-NOTES-25-fence-read
note: Text in a code fence would be read as prose.

name: STE-NOTES-26-quote-unnamed
note: A report would quote a stand-in where the writer wrote a name.

name: STE-NOTES-27-exit-0
old:
for (const f of findings) console.log(`- ${f.message}`);
  return 1;
new:
for (const f of findings) console.log(`- ${f.message}`);
  return 0;
note: The check would pass with findings.

name: STE-NOTES-28-edit-unread
note: An edited description would not be read again.

name: STE-NOTES-29-tee-swallows
note: The tee would pass a failed check.

name: STE-NOTES-30-template-silent
old: Write them in ASD-STE100 Simplified Technical English (STE-NOTES)
note: The template would not tell the writer the law.

name: STE-NOTES-31-sparse-short
note: The job would check out too little to run the check: desktopRelease.mjs loads app/lib.
